name: Password manager and Credential Management API
plain: Browsers and password managers fill saved logins and let a site read or store a credential.
meaning: A site learns the username the person chose, not the password manager's other entries. The Credential Management API lets a site request a saved credential after a gesture. Reused passwords across sites are the main account risk.

access.persistence: Saved until the person deletes it in the password manager
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can fill your saved login once you pick it, and offer to save new ones
limits.user_action: You tap the username box or Sign in, then choose a saved login
can: Show your saved username and password for that site in a picker
Fill the login form with the account you choose
Offer to save a new login after you sign in
Keep you signed in using what your browser or password manager stores
cannot: See saved logins for other sites
See your whole password manager list; it only gets the entry you pick
Fill in a login without a tap, click or key press on the page
Work the same in every browser; support differs
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge support the Credential Management API. Firefox and Safari fill logins through their own built in autofill instead.

story.what_it_is: Your browser or password manager fills in saved logins, and a site can ask for one.

marketing.name: Passwords app and AutoFill
marketing.pitch: Apple presents saved passwords and passkeys as easy to fill across iPhone, iPad and Mac.

story.for_you: You tap a login box and your saved username pops up. One tap fills the password. You may also see an offer to save a new login after you sign up.
story.for_makers: Easy autofill means fewer abandoned sign ups and fewer 'forgot password' emails. Sites mark their forms with the right labels so managers can fill them, and they can safely offer to store the new login.

use_cases.example: A returning shopper taps the email box on a store checkout and the saved login fills in, so they buy before they change their mind.
A player returns to a game store or launcher login page and one tap fills the account, getting them to a new release quickly.
A streaming site shows a saved profile so a person can sign in on a smart TV browser or laptop without typing a long password.
A bank page marks its fields so the password manager fills them safely and warns when the page is not the real domain.
A new hire signs in to many work web apps in a day, each filled in by the manager.
Security teams use leaked password checks in the manager to nudge users to change reused passwords.

risks: Fills on lookalike pages if careless

technical_bounds: Fields are filled only after a click or chooser

abuse: Credential stuffing when passwords are reused
